newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas prices crater ahead of weekend.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas prices crater ahead of weekend.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices cratered Friday in lackluster interest, with Midwest and Texas values leading the way on forecasts for more moderate temperatures by the weekend and early next week.
"It was a complete meltdown in the cash," said one Texas-based trader, noting near-term forecasts for above-normal weather in Texas and the southern plains.
In the Midcontinent, prices plunged by $1.25 to the $3.50s/mmBtu, more than 60 cents below January indices.
Traders said growing storage coupled with an expected break in the recent Arctic wave helped trigger the selloff.
But forecasters differed on what followed the warmup, with some predicting another Arctic front by next weekend.
Gulf Coast prices slumped more than 80 cents to the mid-$3.80s, more than five cents under index.
South Texas weekend values tanked almost $1 to the high-$3.60s, but traders said relatively low producing region storage left the area vulnerable to weather-related spikes.
In west Texas, Permian prices fell by $1.25 to the $3.35 area, about 85 cents under January 1 levels.
In the East, where storage was in fairly good shape but the worst of the cold was just kicking in, New York city gate prices held relatively steady in the low-$6.00 area.
